paragraphs: Yep
With subagents it's … outright; without them — gorgeous by comparison
I think they haven't advanced at all in understanding how to make different sessions work together efficiently
But there's no turning back now, since in every single interview researchers from the top labs talk of nothing but the future belonging to agent swarms
That, like, the human brain is also not one system but a heap of systems working together, etc.
But it's one thing to … about it and another to make it work
For now subagents are just another session that got … and a little bit of context and a shriveled prompt that doesn't even account for the specifics of prompting models
And then the mother session reads a brief retelling of what happened in the subagent's session, hoping it can fully understand what the … it did/saw there
Because the mother session is simply physically incapable of reading in full all the sessions of all its subagents and reasoning over them as if it had been there itself
Knowing and understanding all this, it's not at all surprising that subagents don't work and spoil the result =)
Although before it seemed to me, …, now that's power, my electronic employee hires dozens more for free
And together they assemble a whole stadium of …
So why the hell do you keep doing it?
I played around just a tiny bit and understood right away that models can't orchestrate
Like, for the same reasons they can't work with subagents
Only even worse, since the difference in harnesses gets layered on top there too
Factory ones
It seems to me the problem for many is that they sit and wait for this … to start one-shotting by itself)
… you'll never one-shot anything with an LLM
I've really been … since March and every week there's big progress
But there was never a single one-shot anywhere in it
Vibe-coding is grinding it out; as long as people evaluate the LLM and themselves in it by the principle “I gave it a task and it doesn't work at the end” — it'll be movement in fog)
When you no longer expect anything of the sort from an LLM, you can start structuring the fog somehow, laying it out into systems, managing expectations)
I already understand that on a task of type X I'll be … for 1 to 3 weeks
With a task of type Y, 3 days
Etc.
If it's a tiny piece purely for demonstrating to yourself, you can one-shot it, but very rarely, and you keep one … in mind that in the end it won't be even close to what's needed
Even a working pre-alpha closed personal MVP isn't one day for anything useful
You have to work only through Plan mode all the time:)
Nope
By the way, a funny sudden moment:
Astra drew design very …, which was disappointing, but…
It's simply incapable of inventing it, of creating a design project. It comes out as boring, hunched ….
However, if a design project has already been created by someone (in my case that's Kimi), then Astra becomes extremely good at editing it!

Sol couldn't do that; it outright broke other people's work. Astra extends/edits someone else's base very neatly; I've been playing with this in a separate session for the second day now — pure pleasure.
The delightful flow is this:

1) Get the design in Kimi.ai to roughly what we need; no need to fully polish, because that's very … and now doesn't make much sense; the main thing is that the essence is drawn as it should be, the notional 80% that takes 20% of the time.

2) Give a zip of the files to Astra Medium via Plan Mode, ask it to think the implementation through properly and jam the design in (in the piece I'm working on this took Medium ~3 hours after accepting the plan).
3) Astra stretches Kimi's designs on very tolerably, which means it would've done no worse with a Claude Design design, I suppose.

As a result we have the stretched-on design, and we can walk right through the pages, take photos, and describe our thoughts and reasoning in the freest possible format, throw them into the queue and move on.

On some pieces Astra Medium works 3 minutes, on some 10, on others an hour. But however long it works there, it's simply … convenient, because you don't have to look back. I already have 10–12 such edits hanging in the queue in one session; the flight is gorgeous.
In Kimi design is made gorgeously, but three things there are just wildly … infuriating and spoil everything:
1) No proper way to queue tasks. You have to wait until the previous scope is finished.
2) Kimi is dumb and regularly errs and then “I thought you meant not this screen but that one over there”

3) All of this happens … knows where; Kimi has access only to GitHub there, it regularly drops, you can work only on mock data. Whereas Astra grills right in prod. That gives a feeling of gigantic satisfaction, since you're actually improving something in prod every few minutes, which we've lacked for so long with all these wretched AGI … with which coding became harder, …, not easier.
But Kimi draws best of all, of course. Checked — Opus and Fable still suck compared to it. And if you ask any model who's the coolest in design and web design these days — they point at Kimi.
Claude Design reacts smarter than Kimi, using the design harness is pleasant, but again — … knows how the queue works, and the same excommunication from the repo and the DB.
You can still sometimes throw Codex a “Bro, can you please, while I go for a walk, double-check everything we … today and make sure there are no bugs — if there are, please fix them.”
And it'll fix bugs not only in the design but in the very features the design is wrapped around, if you ask right;)
I was dealing with this back on version 5.5 and then on Sol too
They're sure that dumber/older models can fall for that
While smarter models have long had a very powerful, constantly replenished OpenAI allergy to prompt injections
Hardcore))))
Seems you're pleasant to deal with)
Astra in places did unreally cool stuff
And in places made a mess
But it hasn't finished yet, keeps wandering around as a character and studying something =)
This is the first model that could at all do anything simultaneously geometrically and logically and consistently in meaning within a scene, etc.
The rest just scattered objects randomly and said something completely different from what I saw with my eyes
This one straight-up describes literarily what it sees
Well, it's Ultima Online
Like, we're trying to understand with a model on a 1997 engine what “decorate the Brit bank” means =)
Actually it's a really good benchmark for AGI =))))
I myself can't fully understand how to decorate the Brit bank. It's a very creative task =)
And rather insane within its meaninglessness)
… after all =)
Play around with Astra
It's blowing my mind right now, seriously
In short, the British bank has a roof
Usually on shards they either placed a tile that teleports you onto it
Or attached a staircase, but that's already serious terraforming
In the end Astra came up with placing a beautiful crystal that you double-click to fly up to the roof
I've never even seen that once — it's straight-up its own invention
And the most interesting part
The crystal is placed somehow, like, clumsy
I thought it was because it made a mistake, neuro-slopped it
I ask, like, why is the crystal exactly there?
And it goes, well, at the Brit bank the whole shard crowd usually hangs out
And a heap of people will be running around there if the shard is successful
It's not the prettiest place in the bank for a crystal, but the most effective for people
Because there's no other point where it's most convenient to crowd and yet get access to the roof teleport
The trick is that this is an absolutely correct statement
Which I'm not sure I'd have figured out myself, and then would have just kept moving that crystal
In short, the shard is going to happen now, I reckon
I'll also get the hang of queuing many tasks to Astra on UO, and it'll be possible to finish everything without which I was sick of using such a shard, and we'll … brawl there =)
Ultima is the best game in history =)
Today on my run I listened to the former lead designer of World of Warcraft and Overwatch, who toiled at Blizzard for many years
For 5.5 hours the guy talked about his life and profession
And several times idolized Raph Koster, who actually made UO what it is)
Thereby finally proving my thesis that WoW was completely … from UO no matter what
And simply moved into 3D, casualized for … so as to skin more dough off them)
… I'm … of course
Pegasus Drinking From The Night
At last the answer has been found to the question of whether a robot can make a work of art
The black guy definitely doesn't have to rap for it here now
Like, so that everyone who doesn't understand what UO is gets it:
Out of thousands of objects Astra created a composition, selected objects, chose colors, and this sculpture is about 24 tiles, and it's like a starry lake of night from which a … pegasus drinks

And all of it is also named poetically. It named every object, and even the textures themselves if you click on them; everything has beautiful starry names (it also chose the star theme itself, by the way)
I said “whatever, I don't … care”
Read Postmortems if you have time
Raph Koster wrote it, actually
He describes there how they grinded on Ultima and essentially were the first in the world to do a heap of things, mostly without even understanding what they were doing
But then when they looked at all of it they went … themselves
And sat down to play it themselves)))
Yeah, actually I haven't yet understood why people turned on it so harshly
It doesn't one-shot a lot, of course, but it's … so many times cooler than the salty one and everything before it, all the more, that…
Well, it's just not comparable at all)

It simply works for me all day on medium and does everything I need quickly and powerfully. I've already got the hang of when to ask it once and when three times to recheck itself (you just put it in the queue) and fix what's left — in the end the task renders to near perfection practically by itself
By the way, funny — everyone complains, like, … Astra eats hard. Well yes, but over today I never once left the computer, and observed how OpenAI is actively working on that))))

If yesterday my Max devoured the subscription in 4 hours with ONE SESSION (with agents, true), and Medium was eating about 6–8% an hour on one session, then today I clearly saw the model eat less with every hour, and for the last 6 hours I've had four parallel sessions running, one on Max, three on Medium, and in those 6 hours the model ate about 20% of weekly.
Like, yesterday it would have eaten one and a half full weekly limits in that time:)

I'm even curious what the equilibrium point will be in the end, but if it's like now, then it's a very cost-effective model, and at this rate I simply won't be able to cognitively consume more than three subscriptions a week =)
Truth is, I'm afraid we'll all soon be collectively discussing this here, because it'll get nerfed no matter what
And in the opposite direction, so that its … inside will be like a Japanese vase
Because for a model of, so to speak, elevated cybercriminal risk, it somehow very … easily picked the password to my UO account half an hour ago
It didn't even ask me, just poked around and, …, went into the database and pulled it out and put it in the updated keychain
All the models before it … my brains completely about whether they were allowed to log in
This one didn't even ask which character — it simply took my main GM character, hacked the password and logged in)
Obviously they're doing calibration over there
I think these were just moments over two days when they dropped it to low

Because I don't know in what world Sol is much smarter than the six for people; it was possibly something episodic that I simply didn't catch in my repos on my tasks, but it's hard to even believe that Sol can do something for anyone even approximately comparably
Though I have a suspicion that most negative reviews are from FOMO streakers who, when a reset is promised, write that they launched something on Ultra to drain the subscription
As if Ultra weren't the most cringeworthy useless piece of … that can never finish anything and will drain 10 subscriptions for … giving nothing in return)
Coding even on High is showing off — on Medium it's pure pleasure)
I've got one research on Max running now, 9.5 hours already
I just … to it, like, report please how things are going
Max is like that in everything, even just in reading without any coding at all =)
In the end I talked with it a bit; turned out it had invented a … way of doing research
The most detailed one
Read 4.9 million records …
Lay them out BY DATABASE
Categorize them that way
And conduct experiments between categories, and some other madness …
In the end we agreed on a completely different approach that, by its assurances, will now take it about two hours…

And the result will be exactly the same; all the … it initially dreamed up, I don't know who could need it or why; my task there is simply to determine all the variants where we stumbled in Codex sessions over the past six months and write them out uniquely in a row, that's all

For example it didn't understand that for this you don't need to read the whole telemetry of every session, it's enough to just read my requests and the summaries of the model's answers, and that's already ten thousand times less volume than the whole telemetry)
Well, not that it didn't understand; it explained to me already and I shared a screenshot — Max's task is maximum splitting, and that task is simply incorrect for many things
I should get a job at OpenAI, help Thibault explain to people on Twitter what's obvious to those who really … into these models …)
By the way, I'm very impressed with how far Astra has jumped forward in its understanding of how documentation should be written, and especially how to describe tasks for AI runners.

If before I had to rewrite literally everything bit by bit to get an even remotely sane runner, now some of the prompts Astra wrote for a couple of brand-new runners… I couldn't even manage to change anything in them.
Moreover — I even asked it to rewrite some of my old runners to see how it would do it, and it did it magnificently.
It's one of two things here:

Either the OpenAI harness out of the box has gained the understanding that when you prompt another model, be even more talkative than with a human, because otherwise the model won't understand and will do something random.
Or Astra treats my Agents.md, riddled with this stuff, more respectfully, and actually does as it's written there.
But most likely — both.

I once said that in the foreseeable future there won't be software in the sense we're used to, since determinism is needed only where there's no AI capable of wielding tools, or its precision is insufficient.

@kirilln0v dug up the benchmarks by which AGI points are awarded, and all sorts of neighboring hard ones, and says there are no tricks there. The tasks are extremely hard; a human … solve them in his right mind. That the neural nets do them proves they're already ahead of us.
But here's one snag: these tasks are all limited by context. It's absolutely tiny compared to the contexts people operate with.

Essentially the next breakthroughs should be in that direction. Like, the current model could already be AGI, but AGI is an elastic concept. If it's a problem of a mathematical nature that fits, with maximum compression, into X — then we already have AGI.
If it goes beyond the context a session can process with maximum compaction — AGI turns into a pumpkin.
But the joke is that it can now genuinely solve its own problems itself) I think from here on we'll see only acceleration, as with everything else related to any science =)
Unfortunately Astra got degraded, and very badly
Today, in 10 hours of work on it and a whole Weekly limit of the $100 subscription, I achieved less than I did a couple of days ago in about forty minutes
It took me about a month and a half to get my market scan of 36 AI runners to produce the result I need ten times in a row on 5 fundamentally different projects.
That makes it a product.

However, I decided to try harnessing Astra, which perfectly, brilliantly codes everything on the first try, to analyze this mechanism of mine and reproduce it by writing it independently from scratch. And it got nowhere. Despite having the option, if it wanted, to simply copy everything of mine that already works and lies right before its eyes.
I got curious and spent a couple of days struggling this way and that to make Astra cope with it at least moderately. Didn't work out.

But then I noticed that even if you ask it to throw out everything it piled up entirely and insert my already finished working module — it can't do that properly. Every now and then it adds a line of its own that looks harmless but breaks the foundation, and the result collapses. And it's incapable of understanding this, even if I explain it in the simplest terms. At some point it goes into blind defense and simply nods along, feigns understanding, but can't.
In the process I got the feeling that with Astra, as with the previous models, one of two things is happening:
Either they haven't yet been trained to create complex compound systems of collective work by different neural nets.
Or somewhere in the invisible harness there's a complex compound prohibition on such activity.
I don't know how else to explain it. Like, the mistakes it makes on this task are so dumb and so elementary to detect that it's hard to believe it really can't figure it out even with my help.
It's especially strange to see this in a model that's supposedly meant to skillfully juggle subagents.
Subagents are essentially the same thing. Especially on a big long task.
This only proves that for the current generation of models, multi-agency is just a marketing word and a way to suck out tokens.
Switch off subagents if you haven't yet: multiples of savings, nothing will get worse, and things will get better:)
And if a piece of your product is the complex compound activity of a collective of neural nets — strength to you)

I now understand that any complex compound runner, even on 3 neural nets and ~2 hours of their work together on some creative task, is many weeks. You can't saddle such a feature in one charge, because there's an insane number of things you have to write with your own hands there; the neural net won't do it for you.
Opus is of course a … schizoid =)))
Hadn't used it in a while, gave it the little task of knocking out a reliable updater for the DeepSeek Harness
It's simply been dancing around it for 15 minutes now, and talking to itself very funnily)

… it's already rewritten the whole file in full twice, and then goes, …, but that was already there, so why did I write everything all over again? Hmm. Hmm. Is this right? Or good? Who can tell me? But I'm alone here. Oh. So what am I to do then? Hmm, I'll try once more!
That's roughly how I perceive what it's inferring there)
Astra, by the way, weaned me off these whisperings really fast; it's just unusual to watch now)
